title: Introduction to betaregscale
text: betaregscale package provides maximum-likelihood estimation beta regression models responses derived bounded rating scales. Common examples include pain intensity scales (NRS-11, NRS-21, NRS-101), Likert-type scales, product quality ratings, instrument whose response can mapped open interval (0,1)(0, 1). key idea discrete score recorded bounded scale carries measurement uncertainty inherent instrument. instance, pain score y=6y = 6 0–10 NRS exact value rather represents range: rescaling (0,1)(0, 1), observation treated interval-censored [0.55,0.65][0.55, 0.65]. package uses beta distribution model data, building complete likelihood supports mixed censoring types within dataset.

title: Introduction to betaregscale
text: package supports three reparameterizations beta distribution, controlled repar argument: Direct (repar = 0): Shape parameters =μa = \mu b=ϕb = \phi used directly. rarely used practice. Precision (repar = 1, Ferrari & Cribari-Neto, 2004): mean μ∈(0,1)\mu \(0,1) precision ϕ>0\phi > 0 yield =μϕa = \mu\phi b=(1−μ)ϕb = (1-\mu)\phi. Higher ϕ\phi means less variability. Mean–variance (repar = 2): mean μ∈(0,1)\mu \(0,1) dispersion ϕ∈(0,1)\phi \(0,1) yield =μ(1−ϕ)/ϕa = \mu(1-\phi)/\phi b=(1−μ)(1−ϕ)/ϕb = (1-\mu)(1-\phi)/\phi. ϕ\phi acts coefficient variation: smaller ϕ\phi means less variability.

text: Beta Regression Interval-Censored Scale-Derived Outcomes betaregscale package provides maximum-likelihood estimation beta regression models responses derived bounded rating scales (e.g., NRS-11, NRS-21, NRS-101, Likert scales). Observations treated interval-censored (0, 1) scale--unit transformation, likelihood built beta CDF evaluated interval endpoints. package designed situations recorded score carries measurement uncertainty inherent instrument. example, pain score 6 (0-10) NRS scale interpreted lying interval [5.5, 6.5] rescaling (0, 1). complete likelihood (Lopes, 2024, Eq. 2.24) supports mixed censoring types: uncensored, left-censored, right-censored, interval-censored within dataset. ] (f()) (F()) denoting beta density CDF.

title: Beta Regression for Interval-Censored Scale-Derived Outcomes
text: Mixed censoring support: complete likelihood handles four censoring types simultaneously: exact observations (δ=0\delta=0), left-censored (δ=1\delta=1), right-censored (δ=2\delta=2), interval-censored (δ=3\delta=3). Fixed variable dispersion: model scalar ϕ\phi let depend covariates via second linear predictor (y ~ x1 + x2 | z1). Mixed-effects support: brsmm() fits Gaussian random-intercept models (random = ~ 1 | group) via Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood. High-performance C++ backend: log-likelihood numerical gradient compiled via Rcpp/RcppArmadillo fast, numerically stable estimation. Flexible link functions: logit, probit, cauchit, cloglog mean; logit, log, identity, sqrt, inverse, others dispersion. Three reparameterizations: direct (0), Ferrari–Cribari-Neto precision (1), mean–variance (2). betareg-style S3 interface: print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik, AIC, BIC, nobs, formula, model.matrix, fitted, residuals, predict, confint, plot methods. coef() vcov() methods accept model = c("full", "mean", "precision"). Diagnostic plots: six residual diagnostic panels base R ggplot2 backends, including half-normal envelope plot. Censoring summary: brs_cens() provides visual tabular summaries censoring structure. Simulation toolkit: brs_sim() supports fixed- variable-dispersion Monte Carlo studies via one- two-part formulas. Analyst toolkit: brs_bootstrap(), brs_marginaleffects(), brs_predict_scoreprob(), brs_cv(), brs_table() uncertainty quantification, interpretation, model validation.

title: Fit a mixed-effects beta interval regression model — brsmm
text: conditional contribution observation follows mixed censoring likelihood used brs: \(\delta=0\): exact contribution via beta density, \(\delta=1\): left-censored contribution via beta CDF, \(\delta=2\): right-censored contribution via survival CDF, \(\delta=3\): interval contribution via CDF difference. group \(\), random intercept \(b_i \sim N(0, \sigma_b^2)\) integrated numerically. "laplace": Uses second-order Laplace approximation     conditional mode. Fast generally accurate \(n_i\) large. "aghq": Adaptive Gauss-Hermite Quadrature. Uses n_points     quadrature nodes centered scaled conditional mode curvature.     accurate Laplace, especially small \(n_i\). "qmc": Quasi-Monte Carlo integration using Halton sequence.     Uses qmc_points evaluation points. Suitable high-dimensional     integration (future proofing) checking robustness.

title: Fit a mixed-effects beta interval regression model — brsmm
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(123) g <- 15 ni <- 8 id <- factor(rep(seq_len(g), each = ni)) n <- length(id) x1 <- rnorm(n) b <- rnorm(g, sd = 0.5) eta_mu <- 0.2 + 0.6 * x1 + b[as.integer(id)] mu <- plogis(eta_mu) phi <- plogis(-0.2 + 0.2 * x1) shp <- brs_repar(mu = mu, phi = phi, repar = 2) y <- round(stats::rbeta(n, shp$shape1, shp$shape2) * 100) d <- data.frame(y = y, x1 = x1, id = id)  fit_mm <- brsmm(y ~ x1, random = ~ 1 | id, data = d, repar = 2) fit_mm #>  #> Call: #> brsmm(formula = y ~ x1, random = ~1 | id, data = d, repar = 2) #>  #> Mixed beta interval model (Laplace) #> Observations: 120  | Groups: 15  #> Log-likelihood: -499.3888  #> Random SD: 0.2205  #> Convergence code: 0  # }

title: betaregscale 2.6.3
text: Revised expanded core vignettes (brs-intro, brs-analyst-tools, brs-mm) stronger mathematical exposition, explicit likelihood pieces censoring type, clearer inferential interpretation analysts. Updated vignettes README prioritize package’s important analyst-facing functions: brs_bootstrap(), brs_marginaleffects(), brs_predict_scoreprob(), brs_cv(), brs_table(). Added revised bibliographic references validated DOI metadata dual online source verification links vignettes/README. Re-rendered vignettes rebuilt documentation website (pkgdown) keep articles reference pages synchronized current API.

text: Improved numerical stability brsmm() refining optimization control starting values. Updated simulate() method better handle edge cases random effects simulation. Enhanced methods.R better compatibility downstream packages.

title: betaregscale 2.6.0
text: Added brsmm() mixed-effects beta interval regression Gaussian random intercepts (random = ~ 1 | group) using Laplace-approximated marginal likelihood. Added C++ mixed-model likelihood core: .brsmm_loglik_laplace_cpp() .brsmm_group_modes_cpp(). Added first S3 interface brsmm objects: print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik, AIC, BIC, nobs, fitted, predict, residuals.

title: betaregscale 2.6.0
text: Added test-brsmm.R mixed-model fitting prediction tests. Corrected author name spelling package metadata/documentation: José Evandeilton Lopes.

title: betaregscale 2.5.0
text: Added brs_table() compare one fitted brs models single table logLik, AIC, BIC, pseudo-R2, censoring composition. Added brs_marginaleffects() average marginal effects mean precision submodel, optional simulation-based uncertainty intervals. Added autoplot.brs() ggplot2 diagnostics type = "calibration", type = "score_dist", type = "cdf", type = "residuals_by_delta". Added brs_predict_scoreprob() obtain predicted probabilities original integer score scale. Added brs_cv() repeated k-fold cross-validation brs models fold-level predictive metrics (log_score, rmse_yt, mae_yt).

title: betaregscale 2.1.1
text: delta argument simulation functions: betaregscale_simulate() betaregscale_simulate_z() gain delta argument (default NULL) forces simulated observations specific censoring type: 0 (exact), 1 (left), 2 (right), 3 (interval). enables targeted Monte Carlo studies analyst controls censoring structure. delta non-NULL, actual simulated values (y_raw = rbeta(n, , b)) preserved scale grid, forced censoring indicator passed check_response() vector. ensures observation retains covariate-driven variation observation-specific endpoints. returned data frame carries attr(, "bs_prepared") = TRUE betaregscale(), betaregscale_loglik(), fitting functions use pre-computed left, right, yt, delta columns directly, bypassing automatic boundary classification. Without attribute, fitting pipeline re-classify response y column alone, ignore forced delta. delta argument check_response(): accepts integer vector pre-specified censoring indicators, overriding automatic boundary-based classification per-observation basis. endpoint formulas adapt non-boundary observations: distinction boundary non-boundary observations essential: delta = 1 forced non-zero y, upper bound uses actual y value ((y + lim)/K) rather fixed boundary formula (lim/K). preserves information content observation. Observation-specific endpoints bs_prepare(): internal .compute_endpoints() helper now uses adaptive formulas check_response() analyst-forced left/right censoring non-boundary scores. Previously, delta = 1 always produced right = lim/K delta = 2 always produced left = (K - lim)/K, regardless actual y value.

title: betaregscale 2.1.1
text: Simulation forced delta = 1 delta = 2: internal .build_simulated_response() helper previously replaced y values boundary values (y_grid = rep(0, n) delta = 1, y_grid = rep(ncuts, n) delta = 2). produced degenerate data every observation identical endpoints (e.g., left = 0.995, right = 0.99999 delta = 2), destroying covariate-driven variation making regression fitting impossible. fix preserves actual simulated grid values (y_grid = round(y_raw * ncuts)) passes forced delta vector check_response(), computes observation-specific endpoints using actual y values. Missing "bs_prepared" attribute simulation output: delta forced, simulation functions mark output attr(, "bs_prepared") = TRUE. result, betaregscale() re-classify response via check_response(), silently overwriting forced delta automatic boundary rules. attribute now set correctly.

title: betaregscale 2.0.1
text: bs_prepare() data preprocessing: new analyst-facing function validates, classifies censoring, rescales raw data model fitting. Supports four flexible input modes: score-, score + explicit delta, interval endpoints NA patterns, analyst-supplied left/right bounds. Prepared data automatically detected betaregscale(). Internal helper .extract_response() enables transparent detection bs_prepare()-processed data across fitting, log-likelihood, starting-value functions. censoring_summary() now also accepts data frames bs_prepare(). New vignette section documenting four data preparation modes.

title: betaregscale 2.0.1
text: Fixed potential row-indexing bug bs_prepare() receives subset data frame non-sequential row names. Output now always sequential row names (1:n).

title: betaregscale 2.0.0
text: Removed dependency bbmle. model fitting now uses stats::optim() directly analytical gradients via C++ backend. betaregscale_bbmle() function removed. cumulative parameter replaced delta indicator vector, supports mixed censoring types within dataset. Parameter dados renamed data across functions. Simulation functions renamed: betaregscale_simula_dados() now betaregscale_simulate(), betaregscale_simula_dados_z() now betaregscale_simulate_z().

title: betaregscale 2.0.0
text: Mixed censoring support: complete likelihood (Eq. 2.24) now handles four censoring types simultaneously: exact (δ=0\delta=0), left-censored (δ=1\delta=1), right-censored (δ=2\delta=2), interval-censored (δ=3\delta=3). C++ backend rewrite: log-likelihood analytical gradient functions rewritten C++ (RcppArmadillo) numerically stable, high-performance evaluation. betareg-style S3 interface: coef() vcov() now accept model = c("full", "mean", "precision") argument. New S3 methods: nobs(), formula(), model.matrix(), confint(), plot(). confint() provides Wald confidence intervals based asymptotic normal approximation (z-test, t-test). plot() method six diagnostic panels (residuals vs indices, Cook’s distance, residuals vs linear predictor, residuals vs fitted, half-normal envelope, predicted vs observed) base R ggplot2 backends. censoring_summary() function visual tabular summaries censoring structure, base R ggplot2 backends. predict() expanded five types: "response", "link", "precision", "variance", "quantile". Supports newdata fixed variable dispersion models. residuals() supports five types: "response", "pearson", "rqr" (randomized quantile residuals), "weighted", "sweighted". summary() output now shows separate coefficient tables mean precision submodels Wald z-tests.

title: betaregscale 2.0.0
text: Fixed Pearson residual computation correctly dispatch reparameterization type (repar 1 vs repar 2). Fixed predict() newdata variable-dispersion models. Fixed p-values use pnorm() (standard normal) instead pt() (Student-t), consistent Wald inference theory (Eq. 2.34–2.35).

title: betaregscale 1.1.1
